title: Teen CEO Says Everyone Should Code
main_content:
What does the average 15-year-old do with her free time? Most teenagers are hanging out with friends. But Swetha Prabakaran is different. She enjoys spending her time making the use of technology easier for all.

It’s called coding. So exactly what is that?

“Coding, in the simplest terms, is just you telling a computer to do what you want. … You’re telling a computer to do something and just like we write in English a ‘to do’ list or directions, you write a language for computers.”

Swetha Prabakaran loves to code.

A junior at top-rated Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology, in Virginia, Swetha Prabakaran learned about coding while taking a computer programming class.

Swetha is the founder of Everybody Code Now! The non-profit works to empower the next generation of youth to become engineers, scientists and entrepreneurs.

In September of this year, Swetha was honored at the White House as one of 11 young women named “champions of change,” for her work as the founder of Everybody Code Now. She was one of two 15-year-olds to receive the award.
